description: Reference for using DAG nodes as LLM-callable tools inside an llm_call's tool_configurations. Complements node_configurations.json (which documents nodes as DAG nodes) by focusing exclusively on the tool-calling perspective: how to declare each node type as a tool, what fields are fixed vs LLM-visible, and complete ready-to-use examples.

tool_configurations.summary: A map on any llm_call node that registers DAG nodes as LLM-callable tools. Keys can be semantic names ('search_flights') or UUIDs (generated by frontends) — both work because the engine uses the 'name' field inside each entry as the effective tool name shown to the LLM.

name.description: Tool name shown to the LLM. Use descriptive function-style names (e.g. 'search_flights'). The engine uses this field — the map key is only a fallback when 'name' is empty.

description.description: What the tool does and when to use it. No need to add general 'always call this tool' rules — the engine auto-injects a tool-use instruction block into the system prompt.

node_type.description: DAG node type to execute when the LLM calls this tool. Must be a registered node type.

node_schema.description: RECOMMENDED parameter strategy. A flat map of field names to NodeSchemaField objects. Fields with 'fixed' are hidden from the LLM. Fields without 'fixed' are exposed to the LLM with their type, description, and constraints. Container fields (type='object') support nested 'properties' for mixed fixed/dynamic sub-fields.

NodeSchemaField.fixed: any — if present, field is hidden from LLM and always set to this value. Supports '${context.key}' and '${ENV_VAR}' resolution.
NodeSchemaField.type: string — JSON Schema type: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'object', 'array'. Required for LLM-visible fields.
NodeSchemaField.required: boolean — whether the LLM must supply this field. Only meaningful when 'fixed' is absent.
NodeSchemaField.description: string — description sent to the LLM. Include format expectations and examples.
NodeSchemaField.pattern: string — regex constraint for the LLM (e.g. '^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$' for dates).
NodeSchemaField.properties: object — nested NodeSchemaField map for type='object' containers. Each child can be fixed or LLM-visible.

fixed_config.description: Static values merged into the node inputs before execution. Supports '${context.key}' and '${ENV_VAR}' syntax. Use with node_schema for fixed non-LLM fields, or alone with '$DYNAMIC' placeholders for simple cases.

dynamic_placeholder.description: Set a string value to the literal '$DYNAMIC' to auto-expose it as a required string parameter to the LLM. Limitation: only works ONE level deep inside a container — body.title works, body.metadata.author.name does NOT. For nested or non-string fields, use node_schema instead.

node_config.description: For toolkit nodes only (e.g. tavily_client). The static configuration passed to the underlying toolkit node at construction time (e.g. api_key, max_calls_per_run). Not exposed to the LLM.

expose_sub_tools.description: For toolkit nodes only. Controls which sub-tools are exposed to the LLM. 'all' exposes every sub-tool the toolkit declares. Specific sub-tool names can be listed as an array to expose a subset. When set, the LLM sees '<alias>__<subtool>' as the tool name (e.g. 'web__search', 'web__fetch').

context.description: Dynamic values injected into node_schema or fixed_config via '${context.key}' syntax. Used to pass runtime values (e.g. auth tokens from upstream nodes) into the tool without hardcoding them.

secure.description: When true, the tool output is hashed before being returned to the LLM — real values (e.g. access tokens) are replaced with safe placeholders like '<value_1>'. The engine resolves placeholders back to real values when used in subsequent tool calls via inject_secrets(). Requires DATABASE_URL and SECURE_VALUES_KEY env vars.

enabled_tools.summary: Optional allow-list that unions with the auto-enabled set. Tools defined in tool_configurations are auto-enabled — you do NOT need to list them here. Use enabled_tools only to: (1) enable built-in toolkit tools (Tavily, etc.) not in tool_configurations, or (2) use '*' to expose every available tool including built-ins.
enabled_tools.auto_enabled_behavior: Every key in tool_configurations is automatically enabled. enabled_tools is additive, not a gate. If all your tools are in tool_configurations and none are built-in toolkits, you can omit enabled_tools entirely.
when_to_use: You have built-in toolkit tools (tavily_client, etc.) alongside tool_configurations entries
You want '*' to expose all available tools including built-ins
You want to dynamically enable/disable tools via an upstream node input
when_to_omit: All your tools are defined in tool_configurations and none are built-in toolkits

use_dynamic_when: Fields are flat (no nesting beyond one level)

node_schema_fixed_vs_fixed_config.summary: Both can hide fields from the LLM, but they serve different purposes. Prefer node_schema+fixed for node fields; use fixed_config for purely operational/static values.

use_when: The field is a node config parameter (e.g. sandbox_mode, method, base_url)
You want the field explicitly present in the schema so its intent is clear
The field co-exists with LLM-visible fields in the same schema object
You want consistent schema documentation for the node
The value is purely operational and has no relevance to the LLM (e.g. api_key, base_url for a known endpoint)
You want a simple, flat override without declaring a full schema entry
Used together with $DYNAMIC placeholders for quick string-only cases

node_schema_fixed_vs_fixed_config.rule: If the field is a node behavioral parameter (affects how the node runs), use node_schema+fixed. If it is a static plumbing value (URL, key, method), fixed_config is fine. When in doubt, use node_schema+fixed — it is always correct.

http_request.summary: HTTP calls to external APIs. The most common node used as a tool. Fixed fields (URL, method, headers, auth) are hidden; the LLM supplies only the dynamic parameters.
special_behaviors: Extra non-reserved input keys with primitive values are automatically added as query params.
bearer_token input maps to the Authorization: Bearer header.
When secure: true in fixed_config, the response is hashed — the LLM never sees real tokens.
reserved_keys (never sent as query params): body, query_params, headers, base_url, endpoint, method, bearer_token, authorization, secure, __colmena_session_id, __node_id, __colmena_resume_answer

GET_with_query_params.description: Search endpoint where LLM provides the query string and optional pagination.

search_products.name: search_products
search_products.description: Buscar productos por nombre. Devuelve lista con id, título y precio.

POST_with_json_body.description: Create endpoint where the LLM provides body fields.

create_post.name: create_post
create_post.description: Crear un nuevo post. Requiere título y contenido.

GET_with_path_param_via_endpoint.description: Fetch a specific resource by ID. Since http_request does not support path template substitution natively, build the endpoint string as a fixed prefix and pass the ID as a query param, OR use $DYNAMIC on the endpoint field.

get_product.name: get_product
get_product.description: Obtener detalle de un producto por ID.

authenticated_GET_with_bearer.description: Protected API. Bearer token is fixed (from env var); LLM only sees query params.

search_flights.name: search_flights
search_flights.description: Buscar vuelos disponibles entre dos aeropuertos en una fecha dada.

secure_token_then_use_pattern.description: Two-tool pattern: first tool obtains a token (marked secure: true so the LLM gets a placeholder), second tool uses that placeholder as the bearer. The engine resolves the placeholder to the real token at execution time.

get_token.name: get_token
get_token.description: Autenticar y obtener un token de acceso. Retorna un placeholder '<value_N>' que debes pasar a search_flights.

search_flights.name: search_flights
search_flights.description: Buscar vuelos. Pasar el placeholder exacto de get_token como bearer_token.

dynamic_placeholder_simple.description: Simple POST with flat body using $DYNAMIC. Avoid for nested objects.
dynamic_placeholder_simple.when_to_use: All fields string + required + flat + 5 or fewer. Otherwise use node_schema.

create_comment.name: create_comment
create_comment.description: Crear un comentario en un post. Proporciona el body y el postId.

sql_query.summary: Execute SQL against a PostgreSQL database. Designed primarily as an LLM tool: the connection, permissions, and guardrails are fixed; the LLM supplies only the 'query' string. Queries are parsed with sqlparser (PostgreSQL dialect) and validated per-statement so multi-statement injections cannot smuggle DDL past a benign first statement. Supports a rich permission model and optional LLM-critic validation.
special_behaviors: When used as a tool, node_schema should fix 'connection_url' and 'permissions', exposing only 'query' to the LLM.
The 'auto_context' field injects live schema information into the LLM prompt automatically when set.
Permission presets: 'read_only' (SELECT only), 'read_write' (SELECT + INSERT + UPDATE + DELETE), 'full' (all including DDL).

Allowed statement types: SELECT/WITH, INSERT (single- and multi-row VALUES), UPDATE (WHERE required), DELETE (WHERE required), CREATE TABLE, CREATE FUNCTION (must ship with COMMENT ON in the same script), COMMENT ON.
Always blocked regardless of preset: DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, CREATE SCHEMA, CREATE INDEX, CREATE VIEW, GRANT, REVOKE. Create schemas/indexes/views via migrations, not via the LLM.
Multi-statement scripts are validated per-statement, so `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE x;` is rejected for the DROP and does not execute.
Multi-row INSERT (`VALUES (a,b), (c,d), ...`) is fully supported for bulk loads; only `statement_timeout_ms` caps it.
Unparseable input returns `Failed to parse SQL: …` and refuses to execute — no lenient string-matching fallback.
tenant_user_id + auto_rls enable automatic row-level security without manual WHERE clauses.

read_only_query_tool.description: LLM can run any SELECT query. Connection and permissions are fixed.

query_db.name: query_db
query_db.description: Ejecutar una consulta SQL de solo lectura. Devuelve filas como JSON array.

query.description: Consulta SQL SELECT a ejecutar. Solo SELECT permitido.

read_write_with_rls.description: Read/write tool with automatic row-level security scoped to the current user.

manage_todos.name: manage_todos
manage_todos.description: Crear, leer, actualizar o eliminar tareas del usuario actual.

query.description: Consulta SQL (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Las filas se filtran automáticamente por user_id.

notes: When a tool's node has a layer-1 guide skill (SKILL.md with node_type: <this_type>), the engine auto-folds its body into describe_tool output and into the tool description in eager/non-lazy. tool_configurations.<name>.skills lists per-tool layer-2 references gated by describe_tool.

socketio_request.summary: Connect to a Socket.IO (WebSocket) server, emit an event with a JSON payload, and receive the response. The real-time counterpart to http_request — use it for event-driven APIs that use the Socket.IO protocol. As an LLM tool, fix url/namespace/event/cookies/timeout_ms in node_schema and expose only the dynamic payload fields the LLM should fill in.
socketio_request.see_also: docs/developer_guide/21_socketio_node.md — full guide with config reference, response patterns, pre_events, and troubleshooting.
special_behaviors: Stateless per execution: each tool call opens a fresh Socket.IO connection, emits, collects the response, and disconnects.
Two response patterns: ack mode (default — server replies via the Socket.IO acknowledgment callback) or wait-event mode (set 'wait_event' to listen for a separate named server event).
All string values support '${ENV_VAR}' resolution, including strings nested inside the payload (resolved recursively).
Errors are returned as an envelope, not exceptions: { success: false, event, error, exception? }. This lets downstream nodes branch on success.

pre_events: optional ordered list of events emitted on the SAME connection BEFORE the main event. Essential for servers that scope state per-socket (e.g., room subscriptions, sessions). On any pre-event failure the node aborts and never emits the main event — the envelope includes 'failed_pre_event' and the 'pre_responses' that did complete.
When in doubt about where to put non-LLM-visible fields, use node_schema with 'fixed' (the canonical pattern) — including the entire pre_events array, which the LLM should never see or modify.

load_canvas_state_with_wait_event.description: LLM tool that loads a canvas in one round-trip. The server replies via a separate broadcast event ('canvas_state_loaded'), so wait_event is set. All connection details are fixed; the LLM only triggers the call (no dynamic fields).

load_canvas.name: load_canvas
load_canvas.description: Load the current canvas state for the environment. Returns all existing nodes, edges, and groups.

mutation_with_pre_events.description: LLM tool that creates a node on a Socket.IO canvas. Because the server scopes mutation broadcasts to the room joined by the socket, the tool emits 'join_environment_room' as a pre_event on the SAME connection BEFORE 'create_node'. The pre_events array is fixed so the LLM cannot modify the auth/setup logic. The LLM only fills in the 'node' object inside payload.

create_canvas_node.name: create_canvas_node
create_canvas_node.description: Create a new node on the canvas. Returns the created node with its generated ID.

node.description: Node object: { type, category, position: {x,y}, data: { label, config? } }

ack_mode_simple.description: Minimal ack-mode tool — no wait_event, no pre_events. The server responds via the acknowledgment callback. Use this when the server's reply for the emitted event arrives via ack and no per-socket setup is needed.

ping_server.name: ping_server
ping_server.description: Send a ping to the realtime server and get back its current load metrics.

pre_events_with_wait_event_per_step.description: Two pre-events on the same socket, each with its OWN wait_event (one authenticates and waits for 'auth_ok', the other joins a room and waits for 'joined_room'), then the main event runs. Demonstrates per-step wait_event and per-step timeout_ms.

send_chat_message.name: send_chat_message
send_chat_message.description: Send a chat message to a private room.

text.description: Message text to send to the room.

tips: Default to node_schema + 'fixed' for url/namespace/event/cookies/timeout_ms — the LLM should never alter connection-level fields.
Use ack mode (omit wait_event) when the server replies via the Socket.IO acknowledgment callback. Use wait_event when the server emits a separate broadcast event as the response.

When the server scopes state per-socket (rooms, subscriptions, sessions), use pre_events to set up that state on the SAME connection before the main emit. Two separate socketio_request nodes will each open a fresh socket and lose the setup.

The pre_events array goes inside node_schema with 'fixed' so the LLM cannot disable or alter the auth/setup chain. Failure of any pre_event aborts the call cleanly with success=false and failed_pre_event.
Inputs override config fields with the same name — useful when chaining: a previous node can dynamically supply 'url' or 'payload' via edges while the rest stays fixed.
On error the node returns { success: false, event, error, ... } instead of throwing. Branch on success in downstream nodes if you want the LLM to react to failures.

tavily_client.summary: Toolkit node — exposes multiple sub-tools under a single alias. The LLM sees '<alias>__<subtool>' (e.g. 'web__search', 'web__fetch'). Use expose_sub_tools to control which sub-tools are available. The node_config block holds the Tavily API key and shared defaults; sub-tool parameters are passed by the LLM at call time.
special_behaviors: Toolkit nodes use expose_sub_tools instead of node_schema. The sub-tool schemas are defined inside the node itself.
Sub-tool names follow the pattern '<alias>__<subtool>' — e.g. if the map key is 'web', the LLM sees 'web__search' and 'web__fetch'.
search_defaults in node_config set fallback values for search calls; the LLM can override them per call.
Items in include_domains / exclude_domains must be strings (array of string).

search.description: Web search via Tavily. Returns ranked titles, URLs, and snippets.

include_content.description: Include full page content. 2-3x credit cost.

fetch.description: Read cleaned text from a URL. Use when you already know the URL.

all_sub_tools.description: Expose both search and fetch under the alias 'web'.

web_tool_id.name: web
web_tool_id.description: Web search and fetch via Tavily. Use web__search to find information, web__fetch to read a specific URL.

web.name: web
web.description: Buscar en la web información actualizada.

api_explorer.summary: Toolkit node — exposes 5 sub-tools that let an LLM discover endpoints in an OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.0 spec and deterministically build a valid http_request config. Sub-tools: load_spec, list_endpoints, search_endpoint, get_endpoint_details, build_http_request. Swagger 2.0 docs are converted transparently to OpenAPI 3.0.3 inside the adapter.
api_explorer.recommended_activation: enabled_tools: ["api_explorer"] — flag-only activation. The 5 sub-tools auto-expand in the catalog with default node_config. Use tool_configurations only when you need a custom alias, expose_sub_tools filtering, or per-instance config (cache_ttl_seconds, etc.).
api_explorer.lazy_loading_note: The framework-level lazy_tool_loading feature (summary/eager per tool, see developer_guide/29_lazy_tool_loading.md) does NOT apply to flag-only toolkits. All 5 sub-tools always appear in the initial catalog. However, api_explorer embodies an application-level 'lazy spec exploration' pattern by design: the LLM calls load_spec (compact summary), then search_endpoint (~5KB matches), then get_endpoint_details (full schema for ONE endpoint). The LLM never injects the full spec (100KB+) into the prompt.
dispatch_flow: LLM emits tool_call with name='api_explorer__<sub_tool>' and arguments=<JSON of LLM args>.
DagToolExecutor::execute_inner splits the name on '__' → alias='api_explorer', sub_tool=<sub_tool>.
Looks up tool_configurations[alias]: HIT uses the explicit entry, MISS calls synthesise_default_toolkit_config(alias) (node_config: None, expose_sub_tools: All).
execute_toolkit parses arguments into inputs map, injects ONLY '__sub_tool' as a reserved discriminator, then calls ApiExplorerNode::execute.
ApiExplorerNode reads conversation_id from inputs (falls back to 'default' if absent — which is always under flag-only) and routes by __sub_tool.
ApiSpecUseCase looks up the spec in SessionRegistry<Arc<SpecCache>>; on miss, fetches + parses + caches.
Background TTL sweeper (60s period) evicts idle (>15min) or aged (>1h) entries from the registry.

data_injection.summary: When dispatched via the toolkit path (which is what flag-only activation uses), execute_toolkit builds the inputs map from scratch and injects ONE reserved key only. The non-toolkit dispatch DOES inject __colmena_session_id and __colmena_agent_session_id, but the toolkit path does NOT.

fields.<llm_args>: Set by LLM. Whatever the model passes in tool_call.function.arguments (url, spec_url, query, params, operation_id, etc.).
fields.conversation_id: NOT injected by toolkit path. extract_conversation_id falls back to 'default'. Cache is effectively process-wide (safe — OpenAPI specs are public + immutable, sharing amortises fetch cost).

api_explorer.see_also: docs/developer_guide/25_web_nodes.md — full guide with ASCII dispatch diagram, cache lifecycle, URL normalization, $ref inlining, error model.
special_behaviors: Sub-tool names follow the pattern '<alias>__<subtool>' — if the map key (or enabled_tools entry) is 'apis', the LLM sees 'apis__load_spec', etc. Under flag-only activation the alias is the literal 'api_explorer'.

Spec cache is per-conversation (SessionRegistry keyed by conversation_id + session_name) with passive TTL sweeping (15 min idle / 1 h max). Inside each SpecCache entry is an LRU per spec_url (default 100).
build_http_request output matches the input shape of the http_request node exactly. Secret headers use the '${SECURE:<ref>}' placeholder.
get_endpoint_details inlines $ref resolution (Gemini-safe — no raw '#/components/...' strings).

flag_only_shortcut.summary: api_explorer is the only toolkit today that can be activated WITHOUT a tool_configurations entry. Setting 'enabled_tools' to include the literal alias 'api_explorer' auto-exposes all 5 sub-tools with a synthesised default ToolConfiguration (empty node_config, expose_sub_tools: All).

activation.effect: Engine catalog auto-expands the 5 sub-tools; enabled_tools matches the 'api_explorer' entry as a toolkit prefix (exact OR 'api_explorer__*'); dispatch synthesises a default ToolConfiguration when no explicit entry exists.

when_to_use: Frontend UX where the user toggles OpenAPI tooling with a single boolean — no per-instance config to surface in the UI.
You want the default alias 'api_explorer' (sub-tools are namespaced as 'api_explorer__*') and the default empty node_config.
You do NOT need to filter the 5 sub-tools — all are exposed.
when_not_to_use: You need a custom alias other than 'api_explorer' — declare an explicit tool_configurations entry and pick your own map key.
You need to filter the sub-tools via expose_sub_tools (e.g. only 'load_spec' + 'build_http_request') — only an explicit entry supports this.
You need per-instance node_config (custom cache_ttl_seconds, max_spec_size_bytes, fuzzy_match_threshold) — only an explicit entry exposes node_config.
You want multiple api_explorer toolkits side-by-side (different aliases for different use-cases).
flag_only_shortcut.reference_graph: tests/graphs/web/api_explorer_petstore_flag_only.json — verified end-to-end with OpenAI gpt-4o-mini + real petstore3.swagger.io spec.

load_spec.description: Download + parse + cache an OpenAPI/Swagger spec. MUST be called before the other sub-tools.

url.description: Public URL to the spec (OpenAPI 3.x JSON/YAML or Swagger 2.0). Git-forge URLs are auto-normalised to raw form.

force_reload.description: When true, invalidates the cached entry and re-fetches. Default false.

list_endpoints.description: Browse endpoints by tag with pagination.

spec_url.description: URL of the previously-loaded spec (accepts the input URL or the resolved URL returned by load_spec).

search_endpoint.description: Fuzzy search across path, summary, operationId, tags and description.

method.description: Filter by HTTP method (GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE).

get_endpoint_details.description: Return parameters, request body, responses and security for a specific endpoint. Resolves $ref inline.

operation_id.description: operation_id from list_endpoints or search_endpoint. If wrong, the error includes a did_you_mean list.

build_http_request.description: Emit a JSON object with the exact shape of an http_request node input, with SECURE placeholders for auth.

params.description: Flat map of parameter name to value. Path params, query params, and request-body fields all merge into this single object. Default {}.

auth_secret_ref.description: Secret reference. The auth header is emitted as ${SECURE:<ref>} for http_request to resolve later.

flag_only_minimal.description: Single boolean toggle. No tool_configurations entry. Verified e2e against OpenAI gpt-4o-mini + petstore3.swagger.io (commit 99a128f).

explicit_with_custom_alias.description: Explicit tool_configurations entry — needed for custom alias, sub-tool filtering, or per-instance node_config.

python_script.summary: Run a Python snippet as a tool. Two patterns: (A) Fixed code + LLM provides input variables. (B) LLM generates the code itself — use sandbox_mode: 'restricted' to validate it safely.
python_script.see_also: docs/developer_guide/26_python_node.md — full guide with architecture, threading model, troubleshooting.

reserved_keys.description: These three keys are consumed as node configuration and are NEVER injected as Python variables. Every other key in the schema becomes a global variable in the script.

special_behaviors: All inputs except the reserved keys ('code', 'sandbox_mode', 'sandbox_timeout_secs') are injected as Python global variables.
The script must assign its result to a variable named 'output'. Prefer a dict: output = {'count': 5, 'ids': [1,2,3]}. Returning null is allowed by simply not assigning 'output'.

When sandbox_mode is 'restricted': imports are validated against a whitelist (math, json, re, datetime, collections, itertools, functools, string, decimal, statistics); banned builtins (open, exec, eval, compile, __import__) are blocked; execution is capped at sandbox_timeout_secs (default 10s).
When sandbox_mode is 'none' (default): full Python access, no AST check, no timeout. Only use for trusted code, never for LLM-authored code.
On sandbox violation the node returns an error string ('SandboxViolation: ...') the LLM can read and retry with corrected code. SyntaxError is also surfaced.
Markdown code-block wrappers (```python ... ```) at the start/end of the code are stripped automatically — safe to feed raw LLM output into the 'code' field.
JSON objects/arrays passed via inputs become Python dicts/lists. Access with item['key'], not item.key.

fixed_code_llm_provides_variables.description: Pattern A — LLM provides a string; the script (fixed) transforms it. LLM never sees the code.

word_count.name: word_count
word_count.description: Contar las palabras en un texto.

llm_generates_code.description: Pattern B — LLM writes Python code AND passes the data to process as a tool argument. The LLM has already seen the data in a previous tool call (e.g. an HTTP response in its message history) and now passes it back along with the code. sandbox_mode is fixed so the LLM cannot weaken it. The script accesses 'rows' as a Python variable (from the LLM-supplied tool argument).

run_python.name: run_python
run_python.description: Ejecuta código Python para procesar una lista de datos que tú mismo provees. Pasa la lista en el argumento 'rows' y el código en 'code'. Asigna el resultado a 'output' como diccionario. Ejemplo: output = {'active': len([r for r in rows if r['stock'] > 0])}.

code.description: Código Python a ejecutar. Imports permitidos: math, json, re, datetime, collections, itertools, functools, string, decimal, statistics. NO uses os, sys, open, exec, eval. Asigna el resultado a 'output' como diccionario. Ejemplo: output = {'active': len([r for r in rows if r['stock'] > 0])}

rows.description: Lista de objetos a procesar. Pásale exactamente la lista que recibiste de un tool call previo (e.g. el HTTP response de search_products).

notes: In the current architecture, upstream node outputs do NOT auto-flow into a tool call. The LLM must include the data as a tool argument. This means the LLM has already seen the raw data in a previous turn — token cost is the trade-off for this minimal sandbox feature.
For token-efficient tool-to-tool piping (LLM never sees raw data), see the backlog: docs/superpowers/specs/python-tool-ideas-backlog.md.
Reserved keys (code, sandbox_mode, sandbox_timeout_secs) are the python_node config — everything else in the schema (e.g. 'rows') becomes a Python variable in the script.

Always pin sandbox_mode and sandbox_timeout_secs with 'fixed' so the LLM cannot weaken them. Always describe the allowed-imports list in the 'code' description so the LLM stays inside the whitelist on the first try.

fixed_logic_with_secret_constants.description: Variant of Pattern A — a fixed transform that uses constants the LLM should never see. Put the secret constants directly in 'code' as 'fixed', and only expose the user-facing argument.

score_lead.name: score_lead
score_lead.description: Compute a normalized lead score from a raw value 0-100.

tips: Prefer Pattern A when the transform is deterministic and known at design time. The LLM cannot break it.
Use Pattern B only when the transformation is open-ended (filtering, ad-hoc aggregation, JSON reshaping). Always fix sandbox_mode='restricted'.
For tools that need richer Python (numpy, pandas, requests) the python_script node is not the right tool — wrap your service in HTTP and use http_request as a tool.
Test sandboxed graphs locally with: cargo run --bin dag_engine -- run tests/graphs/agents/python_sandbox_tool_test.json

media_nodes.summary: Three nodes for multimedia generation — image_generation (OpenAI gpt-image-1, Google Vertex Imagen 4), image_edit (OpenAI multipart), and tts (OpenAI / ElevenLabs / Google Gemini TTS). All outputs are persisted via OutputStorageRepository, returned as a single { document_id, mime_type, size_bytes, description } handle (Plan B, 2026-05-25, dropped the legacy attachment_id and url fields), and auto-registered in AttachmentRegistry so the agent can re-load them with load_attachment. NEVER passes raw binary bytes to the LLM context — outbound uses the document_id handle, inbound uses '$attachment:<document_id>' placeholders resolved by the engine (only in the http_request node).
media_nodes.see_also: docs/developer_guide/32_multimedia_generation.md — full architectural guide with URL strategy, scrubber, COLMENA_LOCAL setup, and troubleshooting.
media_nodes.architectural_invariant: LLM never sees raw binary bytes. Enforced in three directions: (1) tool outputs include short URL/handle, never base64; (2) LLM passes '$attachment:<key>' to http_request, engine resolves to data: URI before send; (3) DagToolExecutor scrubs data:*;base64,* strings from tool results before returning to the LLM (universal binary scrubber).

url_strategy_by_storage_adapter.description: All three media nodes return the same JSON shape (document_id only) regardless of storage mode. The LLM no longer receives a url at all (Plan B). Internally the storage_key/read_url differ per adapter; consumers resolve document_id → renderable URL via a dedicated backend endpoint (join against conversation_attachments).

modes.LocalHttpStorageAdapter (COLMENA_LOCAL=t: internal read_url = http://127.0.0.1:<port>/files/<uuid>.<ext>. Bytes also on disk under COLMENA_LOCAL_STORAGE_DIR. Not exposed to the LLM.
modes.HttpCallbackStorageAdapter (COLMENA_LOCA: internal read_url = signed GCS read URL (https://storage.googleapis.com/...?X-Goog-Signature=...). Not exposed to the LLM.
modes.LocalCacheStorageAdapter (unset, in-memo: internal handle = 'local://<uuid>'. Bytes only in process RAM. Not exposed to the LLM.

image_generation_tool.description: Expose image_generation as 'generate_image' tool. Provider/model/api_key/size all fixed; LLM only controls the prompt.

generate_image.name: generate_image
generate_image.description: Generate a brand-new image from a text prompt using gpt-image-1. Returns { images: [{ document_id, mime_type, size_bytes, description }], provider, model } (Plan B dropped attachment_id and url). The 'document_id' is the stable handle — pass it to load_attachment to inspect, or to '$attachment:<document_id>' in an http_request body to ship to a webhook.

prompt.description: Detailed text prompt describing the image to generate.

image_edit_tool_chained_via_attachment_i.description: Expose image_edit, intended to chain from a previous generate_image output. KNOWN GAP (Plan B, 2026-05-25): the LLM-driven gen→edit chain is currently BROKEN. Plan B dropped the legacy 'url' field from generate_image/image_edit/tts tool results — they now expose only 'document_id' (an opaque id like 'img_image_0_ge0png'). But image_edit.fetch_image (image_edit.rs) only accepts source_url in the forms 'local://<key>', 'chat-attachments/<key>', 'data:<mime>;base64,...' or 'http(s)://...'. It does NOT resolve a bare document_id nor a '$attachment:<document_id>' placeholder (the $attachment resolver is wired into the http_request node only, not globally in dag_tool_executor). So an LLM that passes the previous tool's document_id as source_url will fail. Deterministic node-edge chaining that used to forward the old 'url'/storage_key also no longer works since 'url' was removed. Until a fix lands (make image_edit resolve '$attachment:<document_id>' via the attachment registry, or resolve $attachment: in all tool args inside the tool executor), only pass source_url that is an independently-fetchable URL (e.g. an http(s) signed URL or a data: URI not coming from a previous tool result).

edit_image.name: edit_image
edit_image.description: Edit an existing image given a text prompt. NOTE: chaining from a previous generate_image/edit_image tool result is currently a known gap — those results now expose only 'document_id', and image_edit's source_url does NOT resolve a document_id or '$attachment:<document_id>' placeholder. Only pass source_url that is an independently-fetchable 'data:' URI or 'http(s)://' URL. Returns the same shape as generate_image (document_id only).

source_url.description: A 'data:' URI or 'http(s)://' URL of the image to edit. A bare document_id or '$attachment:<document_id>' from a previous tool result is NOT supported (known gap, Plan B).

prompt.description: Describes the desired edit (e.g. 'add a moon in the top-right corner').

tts_tool.description: Expose tts as 'synthesize_speech'. Voice and format fixed; LLM only controls the text. The output's document_id resolves (via a backend endpoint) to an audio URL playable in any HTML5 audio player.

synthesize_speech.name: synthesize_speech
synthesize_speech.description: Convert text into spoken audio using OpenAI tts-1 with the 'alloy' voice. Returns { audio: { document_id, mime_type, size_bytes, duration_ms, description }, provider, model } (Plan B dropped attachment_id and url). Use this when the user explicitly asks for voice or audio output.

http_post_image_via_attachment_placehold.description: Expose http_request as 'http_post_image'. The LLM passes the body with image='$attachment:<document_id>' and the engine resolves the placeholder to a data: URI before the request goes out — the LLM never sees the bytes.

http_post_image.name: http_post_image
http_post_image.description: POST a previously-generated image to a webhook URL. The body's 'image' field MUST be the literal string '$attachment:<document_id>' where <document_id> is from a previous generate_image call — e.g. '$attachment:img_image_0_ge0png'. The engine reads bytes from storage and replaces the placeholder with 'data:image/png;base64,...' before sending. NOTE: the destination is built from base_url + endpoint joined at runtime; this node does NOT accept a single 'url' field.

base_url.description: Full destination URL (e.g. https://hooks.slack.com/...). Joined with 'endpoint' at runtime.

image.description: The literal string '$attachment:<document_id>'. The engine resolves it to a data: URI.

special_behaviors: All media outputs auto-register in AttachmentRegistry with provider=Generated. load_attachment can retrieve them via cross-provider lazy upload (storage.read + upload_streaming to the current provider's Files API).

image_edit.fetch_image accepts source_url in the forms: 'data:' (decode locally), 'http(s)://' (GET via reqwest), 'local://<key>' and 'chat-attachments/<key>' (storage.read). KNOWN GAP (Plan B): it does NOT resolve a bare document_id or a '$attachment:<document_id>' placeholder, so LLM-driven gen→edit chaining is currently broken — generate_image now returns only document_id, which image_edit cannot consume as source_url. The $attachment: resolver is wired into the http_request node only, not globally in dag_tool_executor.

http_request scans body recursively for strings starting with '$attachment:<document_id>' and resolves them via the attachment registry + storage.read before sending. Works at any nesting depth (objects, arrays). last_used_at is touched on a successful resolve (Plan A).

DagToolExecutor applies a universal binary scrubber to tool results: data:*;base64,* strings → '[binary elided: mime=X, encoded_size=N bytes]'; strings >50KB → '[truncated: original_size=N bytes]'. Cap configurable via llm_call.config.max_tool_result_bytes.

TTS audio is registered in AttachmentRegistry but the LLM cannot 'hear' it (vision is image-only). Registration is useful for chaining to http_request via $attachment:<document_id>, not for LLM consumption.

Vertex Imagen uses Application Default Credentials (yup-oauth2): GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS key file → gcloud ADC → GCE/Cloud Run metadata server (runtime SA, no key file needed). Token cached ~50min internally. google_project_id / google_location fall back to GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT / GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION env vars.

crdt_documents.summary: Synthetic LLM tools for real-time collaborative xlsx workbooks (v1 CRDT documents feature). Exposed when an llm_call's config includes the crdt_documents block with an artifact_id. All mutations are in-process against a Yrs-backed document; persisted snapshots are stored locally or in GCS. No tool_configurations needed — the engine auto-creates them when crdt_documents is present. Subsystem F (cross-sheet) adds crdt_doc_list_sheets_of + crdt_doc_import_sheet and extends crdt_doc_get_recent_changes with an optional artifact_id filter.
crdt_documents.how_exposed: Automatically registered when llm_call.config.crdt_documents is present (with artifact_id, storage_backend, etc.). The LLM never sees the artifact_id or storage config — those are internal routing parameters managed by the engine.
crdt_documents.lifecycle: All mutations modify the in-process Yrs document. The ChangeTracker records operations for narration (get_recent_changes). Snapshots are persisted after each DAG run via ArtifactStorage (localfs or gcs).

llm_call_with_crdt_documents.description: llm_call node configured to expose the 6 CRDT tools. No tool_configurations entries are needed — the engine auto-creates them.

config.prompt: Edit the spreadsheet: add a column for Q3 revenue, set cells A1:C5 with sample data, then list all sheets.

crdt_doc_list_sheets.name: crdt_doc_list_sheets
crdt_doc_list_sheets.description: List all sheets in the artifact document. Returns metadata (sheet_id, name) for each sheet. Use this to discover available sheets before read/write operations.

sheets.description: Array of sheet records, each with sheet_id and name.

crdt_doc_read.name: crdt_doc_read
crdt_doc_read.description: Read cell values from a sheet. Optionally specify a range (A1-style notation) to fetch only a region; otherwise returns all non-empty cells.

sheet_id.description: The sheet_id to read from (obtained via crdt_doc_list_sheets).

range.description: Optional range in A1 notation (e.g. 'A1:D10', 'B2:B20'). If omitted, returns all non-empty cells.

cells.description: Map of cell addresses to values (e.g. {'A1': 'Revenue', 'A2': 1000, 'B1': 'Expenses'}).

crdt_doc_set_cell.name: crdt_doc_set_cell
crdt_doc_set_cell.description: Set a single cell to a value. Address in A1 notation.

value.description: The value to set. Can be a string, number, boolean, or null (to clear the cell).

crdt_doc_set_range.name: crdt_doc_set_range
crdt_doc_set_range.description: Bulk set a rectangular range of cells. Supply a 2D row-major array of values.

start_addr.description: Top-left cell address in A1 notation (e.g. 'A1', 'B3'). Defines the starting corner of the range to fill.

values_2d.description: Row-major 2D array of values. Each inner array is one row. All rows should have the same length for a rectangular range.

crdt_doc_add_sheet.name: crdt_doc_add_sheet
crdt_doc_add_sheet.description: Append a new sheet to the document with the given name. Returns the new sheet_id.

name.description: Human-readable name for the new sheet (e.g. 'Q4 Data', 'Archive'). Whitespace is allowed.

crdt_doc_get_recent_changes.name: crdt_doc_get_recent_changes
crdt_doc_get_recent_changes.description: Retrieve a human-readable narration of recent peer changes. Useful for multi-agent or multi-user scenarios to see what other editors did. Optionally specify since_event_id to get only changes after a certain point. Subsystem F adds optional artifact_id to audit a different artifact than the ctx's.

since_event_id.description: Optional u64 event ID. If provided, only changes after this event are returned. If omitted, returns all recorded changes.

artifact_id.description: NEW in F: if set, audits this artifact instead of the ctx's. Default: ctx artifact (subsystem B behaviour).

current_event_id.description: The latest event ID in the document's change history.

narration.description: Human-readable text summarizing recent changes (e.g., 'Peer A set cell B2 to 150. Peer B added sheet Q4Data.').

crdt_doc_list_sheets_of.name: crdt_doc_list_sheets_of
crdt_doc_list_sheets_of.description: Peek at the sheets of any artifact in the registry (cross-artifact, no session ownership check). Use to discover a source_sheet_id before crdt_doc_import_sheet.

artifact_id.description: ULID of the artifact to inspect.

sheets.description: Per-sheet metadata with dimensions, suitable to pick a source_sheet_id.

crdt_doc_import_sheet.name: crdt_doc_import_sheet
crdt_doc_import_sheet.description: Clone a sheet from another artifact into the current artifact (snapshot only — no live link). After import, use crdt_doc_run_python with multi-sheet to analyze. Collisions resolved with ' (2)', ' (3)', … suffix.

source_sheet_id.description: Source sheet id within that artifact.

sheet_id.description: ULID of the newly cloned sheet in the current artifact.

special_behaviors: artifact_id is never exposed to the LLM — the engine uses it internally to route mutations to the correct in-process document.
All v1 tools are auto-registered when crdt_documents is present; you do NOT need to manually add them to tool_configurations.
Mutations modify the live Yrs document in-process with immediate effect (no latency). Snapshots are written after the DAG run completes.
ChangeTracker auto-records mutations for narration; peers can call get_recent_changes to see a human-readable summary of edits.
Storage backend (localfs vs gcs) is transparent to the LLM — all tools work identically regardless of where snapshots are persisted.
If artifact_id points to a previously-saved document, the snapshot is loaded at initialization; edits then accumulate on top.

math_nodes.summary: Arithmetic nodes (add, subtract, multiply, divide, exponential) can be used as tools when the LLM needs to perform calculations on values it already knows. Expose 'a' and 'b' as LLM parameters.

calculate_sum.name: calculate_sum
calculate_sum.description: Sumar dos números. Útil para acumular totales.

research_agent_with_web_search.description: Full llm_call node configured as a research agent with Tavily web search. All three providers work with this configuration.

config.system_message: Eres un asistente de investigación. Busca información actualizada antes de responder.

web.name: web
web.description: Web search and fetch via Tavily

api_agent_with_http_tools.description: llm_call wired with two HTTP tools: a list endpoint and a search endpoint.

config.system_message: Eres un asistente de tienda. Ayuda al cliente a encontrar y listar productos.

search_products.name: search_products
search_products.description: Buscar productos por nombre o categoría.

db_agent_with_sql_tool.description: llm_call with a read-only SQL tool. The LLM can introspect and query a PostgreSQL database.

config.system_message: Eres un analista de datos. Usa la tool query_db para consultar la base de datos y responder preguntas sobre los datos.

query_db.name: query_db
query_db.description: Ejecutar consultas SQL de solo lectura contra la base de datos.

query.description: Consulta SELECT a ejecutar. Solo lectura.

uuid_key_compatibility.description: Frontends often generate UUIDs as tool_configurations keys. Both UUID keys and semantic name keys work identically. The engine always uses the 'name' field inside the entry as the effective tool name — the map key is only a fallback.

example.comment: Both forms work. The LLM receives 'search_products' regardless of the map key.

system_prompt_auto_injection.description: When tool_configurations is non-empty and enabled_tools is active, the engine automatically appends a tool-use instruction block to the system_message. You do NOT need to include 'always use tools' instructions manually.
system_prompt_auto_injection.injected_block_template:
## Tool Use Instructions
You have access to the following tools:
- <tool_name_1>
- <tool_name_2>

Rules:
- ALWAYS use the available tools to answer questions that require real or live data. Never answer from your own knowledge when a tool can provide the data.
- Call the most relevant tool before responding. Do not skip tool calls.
- If a tool call fails, report the error clearly instead of guessing an answer.
- Only respond without a tool call when the user's request is purely conversational and no tool is needed.
system_prompt_auto_injection.implication: Your system_message only needs to describe the agent's role and behavior — the tool instructions are managed by the engine.

deprecated_fields.note: These fields still work for backward compatibility but must not be used in new configurations. Use node_schema instead.

fields.exposed_inputs: Array of input names to expose to the LLM.
fields.parameters: Manual JSON Schema override for tool parameters.
fields.mergeable_fields: Fields where fixed + dynamic values are merged rather than overridden.
fields.field_mapping: Maps each LLM parameter to its destination container field.
